default.notes: Visa-free for 30 days under Executive Order 408; extendable by 29 days (visa waiver) at a Bureau of Immigration office, and further in-country extensions are routine.

groups.notes: Visa-free entry for 30 days under ASEAN arrangements; extendable at a Bureau of Immigration office.
A temporary visitor (9a) visa from a Philippine embassy or consulate is required before travel.

PH.notes: Filipino citizens enter freely with a valid Philippine passport. eTravel registration still applies to arriving Filipinos.

CN.notes: Chinese citizens need a temporary visitor (9a) visa. An eVisa for Chinese nationals has been rolled out at evisa.gov.ph — check current availability, as the programme has been suspended and resumed at times.

IN.notes: Indian citizens holding a valid visa or residence permit for the US, UK, Schengen area, Japan, Australia, Canada or Singapore may enter visa-free for 14 days (extendable by 7). Otherwise a 9a visa is required — an eVisa route for Indian nationals has also been announced. Confirm conditions before travel.

TW.notes: Taiwan passport holders apply online through the official Philippine eVisa at evisa.gov.ph, which was first rolled out for Taiwanese travellers.
